conventions.convention: Calculations use one named inertial laboratory frame and SI units. ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹>0; μ₀ is experimentally determined, without an asserted exact numerical value.

A bounded Cᵏ domain is nonempty, bounded and open, with locally exactly one-sided graph charts; connectedness is not part of the definition. Closure regularity means continuous extensions of the stated interior derivatives.
On a conductor surface n points from conductor into vacuum, while the outward vacuum normal is ν=−n. Consequently σ=ε₀n·E₊=ε₀∂νφ.

The compact conductor model permits a general open ambient region. Its bounded smooth ambient branch additionally requires connected vacuum. Grounded planes and infinite plates are separate noncompact idealizations.
Poisson uses −Δφ=ρ/ε₀. For outward normal datum g=∂νφ, compatibility is ∫ρ+ε₀∫g=0 separately on each connected component.

The capacitance matrix is defined for zero volume source, connected bounded smooth vacuum, and grounded outer boundary. A scalar capacitance C₁₁ refers to driving conductor 1 while grounding every other conductor.
Half-space uniqueness requires zero plane trace, sub-Coulomb pole growth |x−p|w(x)→0, and uniform vanishing at spatial infinity within H.
Electric Cartesian indices are 1,2,3 in the laboratory basis. Moments are about the named chart origin; Qᵢⱼ=∫(3yᵢyⱼ−|y|²δᵢⱼ)ρ. Finite point systems include empty systems and coincident points.

Density support restrictions are almost-everywhere restrictions. The dipole bound applies for r≥2a; the all-order exterior series applies for r>a, without asserting convergence at r=a. Spherical harmonics are real, orthonormal for surface measure of mass 4π, with m=1,…,2l+1.
Distribution pairings are complex bilinear, without conjugation. Singular-source products are not defined; line and noncompact cylindrical-sheet sources require their separately declared model.

The smooth current class is J∈C∞c(Ω;R³), div J=0, extended by zero to R³. Ideal loops, infinite lines and cylindrical sheets are distinct source classes, with their own regularity, symmetry and decay predicate.
The cross product is right-handed. Magnetic moments are m=½∫y×J and, for the declared loop, m=(I/2)∫γ×γ′. Positive circular traversal gives m=Iπa²e₃.

Broad charge-data force assignments and thin-wire coupling are explicitly adopted extensions, rather than consequences of the smooth continuum Lorentz postulate. Only prescribed external fields contribute; self-fields and mechanical dynamics are excluded.

Lebesgue, surface and distributional branches retain Countable Choice. Boundary solvability and capacitance retain full Choice through their trace and solvability suppliers. Finite moment and wire-force calculations distinguish their choice-free branches.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts finitely many bounded smooth conductor bodies with pairwise disjoint closures strictly inside an open ambient region; stationary surface charge, zero conductor-interior field, distributional vacuum Maxwell equations, and a continuous potential constant on each body. In the additional bounded smooth ambient branch the vacuum is required to be connected. Potential data and total-charge data are distinct declared data types; arbitrary solvability is not asserted.

The compact smooth current class consists of J∈C∞c(Ω;R³) with div J=0, extended by zero to R³. A magnetostatic field of such a current is C¹ on R³ and satisfies div B=0 and curl B=μ₀J. Separately defines tangent-loop, infinite-line and cylindrical-sheet distributions and their field admissibility predicate; it asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

Under AC and Countable Choice, on a bounded smooth vacuum domain with finitely many components and smooth ρ, every smooth Dirichlet datum has a unique smooth potential solving −Δφ=ρ/ε₀, also unique in the weak H¹ class. Smooth outward Neumann data satisfying componentwise ∫ρ+ε₀∫g=0 admit smooth solutions modulo componentwise constants. The conductor clause constructs the surface charge and distributional equations; the finite disjoint smooth-interface clause supplies weak transmission existence, smoothness on closed sides and n·[ε₀∇φ]=−σ.

Under AC and Countable Choice, for the compact separated conductor geometry with bounded smooth ambient domain, connected vacuum, grounded outer boundary and zero volume source, define Cⱼₖ=ε₀∫∂Dⱼ∂νφₖ using the unit Dirichlet solutions. For every V∈Rᵐ, φⱽ=ΣVⱼφⱼ, Q=CV, C is symmetric positive definite, and U=(ε₀/2)∫|∇φⱽ|²=½VᵀCV=½ΣVⱼQⱼ. With only conductor 1 driven, C₁₁>0 and U=Q₁²/(2C₁₁).

For a real compactly supported L¹ density vanishing almost everywhere outside the closed ball of radius a>0, defines Q=∫ρ, pᵢ=∫yᵢρ, Cartesian moments ∫yᵢ₁⋯yᵢₗρ and Qᵢⱼ=∫(3yᵢyⱼ−|y|²δᵢⱼ)ρ, all absolutely convergent. Also defines the corresponding finite sums for stationary point charges, including the empty system, and the weighted locally integrable branch. Every moment is about the chart origin.

Under Countable Choice, for J∈C∞c(Ω;R³), div J=0, extended by zero, A=μ₀N(J) is smooth on R³, satisfies −ΔA=μ₀J and div A=0. B=curl A is smooth with div B=0 and curl B=μ₀J. E=ρ=0 and time-independent B,J give a full smooth Maxwell completion. Neither A nor B uniqueness is asserted.

Under Countable Choice, the Newtonian magnetostatic field of a compact smooth conserved current has, at every x∈R³, the absolutely convergent representation B(x)=(μ₀/4π)∫J(y)×(x−y)/|x−y|³dy. For the declared embedded closed C² arc-length loop, mollified tangent-current fields converge with every derivative uniformly on compact sets disjoint from the curve to the stated line integral; its global local integrability, distributional equations and decay are supplied separately by the thin-current lemma.

Under Countable Choice, for real ρ∈L¹(R³) vanishing almost everywhere outside the closed ball of radius a>0, the Coulomb potential has its spherical-harmonic expansion for r>a, absolutely and uniformly on r≥r₀>a, with degree-N tail at most ‖ρ‖₁aᴺ⁺¹/[4πε₀r₀ᴺ⁺²(1−a/r₀)]. Every fixed derivative converges uniformly on exterior compact sets. Degree two is nᵢQᵢⱼnⱼ/(8πε₀r³). Its separate ball branch supplies the unique harmonic potential with prescribed L² angular boundary limit and bounded radial L² norm.

Under Countable Choice, for real ρ∈L¹(R³) vanishing almost everywhere outside the closed ball of radius a>0, φ=ε₀⁻¹Nρ satisfies φ(x)=Q/(4πε₀r)+(p·x)/(4πε₀r³)+R(x) for r≥2a, with |R(x)|≤16a²‖ρ‖₁/(4πε₀r³), uniformly in the exterior region. It asserts no derivative bound for R and no density-theorem application to singular point sources.

Under Countable Choice, for a conductor-model solution with the stated joint one-sided C¹ field regularity and n directed from conductor into vacuum, n·E₊=σ/ε₀, n×E₊=0, ∂nφ=−σ/ε₀, and Qⱼ=∫∂Dⱼσ=ε₀∫∂Dⱼn·E₊=ε₀∫∂Dⱼ∂νφ, where ν=−n. Continuous potential traces equal the prescribed Vⱼ. No charge-data existence or uniqueness is asserted.

Under Countable Choice, if Ω is a bounded Cᵏ domain, k≥1, and D₁,…,Dₘ, m≥0, are bounded Cᵏ domains with pairwise disjoint closures strictly inside Ω, then Ωᵥ=Ω\(∪closure Dⱼ) is a nonempty bounded Cᵏ domain. Its boundary is the disjoint union ∂Ω∪∂D₁∪⋯∪∂Dₘ; its conductor-boundary normal is the negative conductor normal. It has finitely many connected components, each again a bounded Cᵏ domain with its incident boundary components; connectedness of Ωᵥ is not asserted.

Under Countable Choice, for H={x₃>0}, p=ae₃, a>0, and q∈R, φᵢ=(q/4πε₀)(|x−p|⁻¹−|x+ae₃|⁻¹) is harmonic off p, has distributional point source qδp, zero plane trace and decay. It is unique among the stated harmonic competitors with sub-Coulomb difference at p and vanishing at infinity. The separately defined noncompact plane density is −qa/[2π(x₁²+x₂²+a²)³ᐟ²], has total charge −q, and gives the directly verified all-space extension identities.

Under the explicitly adopted external thin-wire coupling, the stated C² arc-length parametrized curve has F=I∫γ′×B(γ) and N=I∫γ×(γ′×B(γ)). For a closed curve and constant external B, F=0 and N=m×B. For a closed curve in |x|≤a, C² divergence-free external B and the stated Lipschitz and quadratic-remainder bounds, F=∇(m·B)(0)+R_F and N=m×B(0)+R_N, with |R_F|≤½|I|La²M₂ and |R_N|≤|I|La²M₁. Open segments require feed/return in a global model.

concerns.concern: The title says 'decaying at the pole', whereas Statement (iii) assumes only |x−p|w(x)→0, explicitly called sub-Coulomb growth in the body. That is the correct condition used by the barrier proof, but the title describes it imprecisely.

The batch-27 cross-batch ledger retains open evidence alleging a 1-based contraction in lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder and missing Parseval justification in lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence. The current remainder statement explicitly uses canonical indices k<3; the current ball lemma F2 and Proof 1.1 explicitly derive Bessel, density convergence and Parseval. These old descriptions need current consumer/producer dispositions under the authorized ledger protocol; their old open status alone does not demonstrate a present mathematical defect.

seams_checked.note: BVP existence F1 and Proof 1.1–1.3 instantiate the bounded smooth elliptic theorem with ε=ε₀I, preserving AC, smooth data, componentwise conormal compatibility and finite disjoint smooth-interface restrictions.

The star-shaped potential citation is explicitly limited to interior regularity. Image arguments use the point-source Coulomb clause; capacitance derives sheet energy locally rather than applying the smooth volume-source energy theorem to sheets.

General multipoles F7 and Proof 2.1, 3.1 and 5.1 preserve the real compact L¹ source, exterior radius, 4π normalization, degree-tail bound and compact derivative convergence. The L² ball branch remains separate. Current supplier bodies address the old index and Parseval objections still described in the batch-27 ledger.

Density expansions use Coulomb clause (c), while the two-charge example uses clause (d) and proves its finite-kernel remainder directly. The smooth full-field interpretation is conditional on the additional smooth-source hypotheses.

The vector potential uses the smooth Newtonian derivative identity componentwise. Magnetic dipole estimates retain smooth conserved compact currents and r≥2a. Biot-Savart explicitly imports global local integrability and distributional equations from the thin-current supplier, independently of off-curve convergence.

Steady-current compatibility preserves the smooth versus distributional regularity distinction. The definition expressly excludes line and noncompact-sheet models from the earlier weak-source class and introduces their separate physical adoption.

RL–LC dynamics Statement (b) and L1 explicitly retain full AC, the compact separated geometry, bounded smooth ambient domain, connected vacuum, grounded outer boundary, zero volume source and one driven conductor. C=C₁₁ and frozen energy Q²/(2C₁₁) are conditional identifications.

Inductance reciprocity F1 states the exact smooth Newtonian vector-potential conclusion for compact conserved currents. Current profiles are numerical SI shapes per ampere; time-varying circuit uses are explicitly frozen configurations, without asserting a full time-dependent Maxwell solution.

The current page and its listed item bodies contain no citation to an owned conductor item or restatement of an owned proposition. Guide-cavity geometry (b) instead declares PEC conditions through the separate material-jump supplier and explicitly excludes deriving box-edge or conductivity-limit claims from that supplier. Thus this declared page prerequisite has no proposition-level citation instance to certify; no overstrong use of an owned conductor theorem was found.

Dipole radiation defines p(u)=∫yρ(y,u)dy about the fixed chart origin and identifies it as the fixed-time analogue of the static moment definition. The consumer assumes smooth compact conserved time-dependent sources and derives its time-dependent identities locally; it does not apply the static exterior expansion as a radiation theorem.
